title: Conversational streaming SLOs: first-token & per-token latency, error-budgeting, and progressive canary gates
creator: Elena Park
description:
PRD summary: Define production-grade SLOs and acceptance criteria for Redwood's conversational streaming endpoints (hosted + dedicated). Focus is on two orthogonal dimensions: 1) first-token latency (time to first byte for a response) and 2) steady-state per-token latency during streaming for interactive use cases. This ticket codifies numerical targets, monthly error budgets, automated burn-rate checks, and a conservative progressive canary rollout plan tied to synthetic traffic and customer cohorts.

Goals:
- Provide clear, measurable SLOs for conversational streaming that reflect user-perceived responsiveness.
- Create deterministic rollout gates that integrate with Console dashboards and the automated rollout engine.
- Ensure early-warning detection (burn-rate) to halt rollouts before customer-visible degradation.

Non-goals:
- Model architecture changes, quantization experiments, or kernel-level optimizations (handled in ENG PRs).
- Per-tenant custom SLOs for this release (defers to follow-up ticket).

Scope changes since kickoff: Added explicit steady-state per-token budgets after perf spike observed in load tests (see comments 2025-11-08). Added synthetic region-localized canary traffic to better emulate tail effects (approved 2025-11-10).
metrics: Availability SLO: 99.95% monthly availability for streaming endpoints (hosts: api.redwood.com, regional endpoints).
Monthly error budget: 0.05% -> ~22 minutes unavailable per 30-day window (used to calculate burn-rate).
First-token latency (interactive small prompt <128 tokens): p50 < 80ms, p90 < 160ms, p95 < 300ms (measured at edge).
Steady-state per-token latency (after first token): p50 < 18ms, p90 < 40ms, p95 < 60ms (sustained streaming for multi-token responses).
Tail/long prompt penalty band: for prompts >1024 tokens, p95 first-token budget relaxed to 500ms (documented exception).
Error classification: 4xx client errors excluded from availability SLO; 5xx + timeouts + truncated streams count as SLO failures.
acceptance_criteria: Synthetic canary tests: internal synthetic traffic (mix: 60% short prompts, 30% mid, 10% long) must meet all latency SLOs over a 72h rolling window before moving to customer beta.
Dashboard readiness: Console shows first-token and per-token time-series, SLO burn-rate alerting, and per-region breakdown in the runtime-1.22 release dashboard.

Automated rollback: When burn-rate > 3x expected for a 30-minute window or >1.5x for 2 hours, the rollout automation must pause and revert traffic by configured step (manual confirmation path documented).
Canary data retention: Synthetic traffic traces (sampled) and kv-cache hit/miss metrics available in logs for at least 14 days for incident triage.
Load test verification: A replicated load test (internal infra) with 2x expected peak QPS for the canary configuration shows no SLO failures for first-token p95 or steady-state p95 over a 4-hour run.
Operational runbook: On-call runbook updated with focused playbook for streaming regressions, including quick rollback steps, model fallback invocation, and customer communication templates.
rollout_gates: Phase 0 - Internal: 0% public traffic. Run 72h synthetic canary, pass metrics -> proceed.
Phase 1 - Closed Beta: 1% of traffic routed to canary cohort (internal + invited customers) for 48h. SLO pass + burn-rate < 1x -> proceed.
Phase 2 - Gradual Ramp: Increase to 10% over 48h in 3 steps (1% -> 3% -> 10%). At each step: rolling 30m burn-rate check (must be <2x) and rolling 3h SLO check (p95 budgets).
Phase 3 - Broad Beta: 50% traffic for 72h. If burn-rate remains <1.2x and no sustained p95 spikes, proceed to GA. Otherwise rollback.
Phase 4 - GA: 100% traffic with continued monitoring. Post-GA: weekly SLO review for 4 weeks and optional throttle policies per tenant if issues surface.
